title: The first superconducting final focus quadrupole prototype of the FCC-ee study

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states field quality is 'excellent, with higher-order multipoles below 1 × 10⁻⁴ units.' However, throughout the rest of the paper (e.g., Table 2 caption: 'They are expressed in 10⁻⁴ units', and statements such as '...are still below 1 unit in the central region' and 'reaching values below 5 units') the term 'units' is itself defined as already representing 10⁻⁴ (the standard accelerator-magnet convention). Appending '×10⁻⁴' to 'units' in the abstract therefore implies a value ~10,000 times smaller than what is reported and discussed elsewhere in the paper, creating an internal inconsistency in the stated order of magnitude of the field quality.

The abstract asserts that the measured multipoles are 'consistent with simulations and room temperature tests,' implying agreement between cold and warm results. However, the body text explicitly states 'The field quality analysis results, although worse than the warm tests, are still below 1 unit in the central region,' directly acknowledging a degradation relative to the warm (room-temperature) measurements. This contradicts the stronger claim of consistency made in the abstract.

The text states: 'The correction is confirmed by comparing coefficients from the coils positioned on the corrected and non-corrected sides as shown in Table 2.' However, the actual caption of Table 2 describes a completely different comparison: 'Comparison of the field quality between the warm and cold (1.9 K) measurements of the CCT quadrupole powered with a current of 5 A and 765 A respectively.' The table as captioned does not correspond to a corrected-vs-non-corrected side comparison, but rather a warm-vs-cold comparison at different currents, contradicting what the text claims the table shows.

predicted_errors.error_location: Cold test description and Field Quality section (both referencing 'Fig. 3')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Fig. 3 is cited twice for unrelated content: first, 'The prototype was placed inside a cryostat with rotating coils, as depicted on the right side of Fig. 3' (describing the cold-test cryostat setup), and later, 'This is illustrated in Fig. 3 with the grooves hosting the conductor diverging from the usual sinusoidal profile that leads to undesired edge effects' (describing the conductor groove layout). These are clearly two different pieces of content (an experimental apparatus photo vs. a conductor-layout schematic) that cannot both be the same single figure, indicating a figure-numbering/reference inconsistency.
